summary: Child chats on other machines (design 2026-10-29), built in steps behind the staged flag hub_remote_children. Step 1, the VM backend lifecycle: the remote bootstrap starts the headless backend and the managed code-server detached (setsid nohup, output in ~/.switchboard-server/server.log), so a tunnel drop, a desktop sleep or a quit no longer ends the sessions on the VM. Each connect reuses a live backend when its pid is still ours, it was started from the installed version (server.version equals version) and its HTTP listener answers within 3 s; otherwise it reaps the backend and code-server as before and starts fresh ones. The ssh session waits on the backend pid, so the tunnel ends when the server dies. The backend now always runs with a token: the bootstrap keeps it 0600 in ~/.switchboard-server/token and prints it once on the ssh channel; the desktop reads it from the tunnel output (never logged), keeps it in memory, sends it in the health probe and gives it to the renderer through a desktop-only IPC call (not the backend host, which also serves phones). The renderer sends it in an auth frame; WsHost accepts the server token in an auth frame with the same scopes as the URL token.

reactNativeIos.reason: Phones never dial a VM's tunnelled backend; they reach the desktop only, or a VM's own TCP listener with the token the operator set, which this change does not touch.

nativeAndroid.reason: Same as iOS: the Android app does not use the ssh bootstrap or the desktop's tunnel, and its IAP path to a VM's TCP listener is unchanged.

storageDataMigration.reason: No database or settings change. The VM gains two flat files under ~/.switchboard-server (token, 0600, and server.version); a missing server.version makes the first connect after the upgrade reap the old foreground server, as every connect did before.

automated: npx vitest run tests/unit/remote-bootstrap-cleanup.test.ts tests/unit/connect-deps.test.ts tests/unit/connection-manager.test.ts tests/unit/ws-host-auth.test.ts --maxWorkers=2: the bootstrap reuses a live server of the installed version and reaps otherwise, starts both processes detached, keeps the token 0600 and prints it once, is valid shell (bash -n); the health probe dials with the token once the tunnel has printed it; the token line is read across stdout chunks; WsHost accepts the server token in an auth frame and closes 4001 on a wrong one.
notExercised: Phones: no change on that path.
